title: Read real FASTA and FASTQ records
intro: Use Biopython sequence objects and standard in-memory file formats. Learn to preserve identifiers and per-base quality metadata.

scientific_context.caution: FASTA/FASTQ records are synthetic and short. No external sequencing run, base caller or verified reference assembly is implied.

chapter_method: Predict → Run → Investigate → Apply → independent Prove → delayed review.

goals.title: Construct Seq and SeqRecord with identifiers
goals.why: A sequence without its specimen identifier loses crucial provenance.
explain: Seq stores nucleotide operations; SeqRecord connects the sequence to an ID and optional description.
The object description is metadata, not a measurement or a claim that the sequence is from a named gene.
The inputs are deliberately synthetic for practice; matching an expected result does not validate a biological interpretation.

worked_example.code:
from Bio.Seq import Seq
from Bio.SeqRecord import SeqRecord
r=SeqRecord(Seq('ATGN'),id='read01',description='synthetic')
print(r.id,len(r.seq))

goals.title: Parse and write FASTA without losing IDs
goals.why: Biological reference files can contain many records, not one long anonymous sequence.
explain: SeqIO.parse(handle,'fasta') preserves record boundaries; SeqIO.write can serialize records back to FASTA.
Joining all FASTA lines without respecting '>' headers merges distinct sources and invalidates coordinate positions.
The inputs are deliberately synthetic for practice; matching an expected result does not validate a biological interpretation.

from Bio import SeqIO
from io import StringIO
print([(r.id,len(r)) for r in SeqIO.parse(StringIO('>a

goals.title: Extract genomic intervals with strand awareness
goals.why: Off-by-one coordinates create biological interpretation errors in amplicon and gene analysis.
explain: Python slices are zero-based half-open [start:end]; reverse-complement only when the requested strand is '-'.
An end coordinate is excluded in Python and must not be treated as a one-based inclusive reference coordinate.
The inputs are deliberately synthetic for practice; matching an expected result does not validate a biological interpretation.

goals.title: Read FASTQ and Phred quality arrays
goals.why: Sequence reads and their quality scores must stay linked by base and read ID.
explain: Biopython SeqIO.parse('fastq') decodes ASCII quality encoding into numeric phred_quality values.
